questions.question: How should I structure the Python port of the three shell scripts?

options.label: Standalone scripts
options.description: Each .sh → one .py invoked directly by its plist, exactly like the existing usage-limit-monitor.py. Pure/decision logic extracted into testable functions + a tests/ suite. Minimal launchd change (swap ProgramArguments), lowest risk for live boot services, matches current repo convention. Leaves usage-limit-monitor.py untouched.

options.label: Full remote_control/ package
options.description: The written PYTHON_PORT_PLAN.md approach: an importable remote_control/ package (config, discovery, supervisor, installer, codex_relay, cli) + folds the already-Python usage-limit-monitor.py in too. Cleaner separation but needs PYTHONPATH/shims in plists and touches a live service for ~zero functional gain.

questions.question: Port codex-relay.sh too? It's a 37-line PATH-setup + exec npx wrapper that was just shipped and verified under launchd.

options.label: Yes, port it
options.description: Honor 'all shells (ok for small ones)' — port to a Python exec wrapper (os.execvp(npx,...)) with identical behavior, then re-verify under launchd (8787 binds, KeepAlive respawn).

options.label: Leave it shell
options.description: Skip it: the plan flags churn risk — re-porting a just-verified live service for near-zero benefit. Port only the supervisor and installer.
